chunks: Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abī Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: Regarding the absent man who divorces, how long must his absence be? He said: "Five months or six months." I said: Is there a limit in it less than that? He said: "Three months."

key_terms.الْغَائِبُ: the absent man, meaning the husband who is away
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ: three months, the shorter limit mentioned
key_terms.غَيْبَتُهُ: his absence, the period during which he is away

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum period of absence for an absent husband’s divorce in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the divorce of an absent husband and the length of absence relevant to that ruling. Imam Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام states that the absence may be five or six months, and that a shorter limit mentioned is three months.
